title: PM Abiy Welcomes Global Health Leaders to Cphia 2026 in Addis Ababa
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has invited African leaders, health experts, and global partners to Addis Ababa for the Fifth International Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA 2026), calling for collective action to build a healthier and more resilient continent.

summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Tigray's dynamic relationship with the modern Ethiopian state has been shaped by a historical paradox and contradiction: Tigray has been both a target of state oppression, betrayal, and genocide and, at critical moments, an influential participant in shaping the Ethiopian state itself. title: U.S. Lawmaker Proposes Trade Incentives to Push Ethiopia, Eritrea Off Conflict Cliff, Toward Peace
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- US Republican Representative Jim Baird has proposed two pieces of legislation seeking to link expanded trade and economic cooperation with Ethiopia and Eritrea to progress toward lasting peace, as tensions between the neighboring countries continue to raise fears of a renewed interstate conflict.

title: Nearly 700,000 Displaced By Moyale Conflict in Southern Ethiopia: Islamic Relief
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Nearly 700,000 people have been displaced by Moyale conflict along Ethiopia's border with Kenya and Somalia, with widespread destruction of homes and disruption of essential services, Islamic Relief Ethiopia said, warning of a deepening humanitarian crisis.

title: Ethiopia, India Seek to Deepen Strategic Trade and Investment Partnership
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia and India have discussed about expanding bilateral trade and investment cooperation, with Ethiopia highlighting opportunities created by its ongoing economic reforms and access to the wider African market.

title: Overnight Drone, Artillery Strikes Reported Around Badme Amid Ethiopian, Eritrean Military Buildup
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Intense overnight drone strikes and heavy artillery bombardments were reported in areas surrounding the border town of Badme, as Ethiopian and Eritrean forces continued building up military positions along their shared border, raising fears of a sustained direct confrontation between the two countries.

title: When Borders Become Battlefields - the Human Cost of Buffering Ethiopia-Eritrea Tensions
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Over the past few months, relations between Ethiopia and Eritrea have frayed once again, casting the shadow of war across their shared border. To defuse this mounting tension, various quarters have floated a familiar prescription: establishing a demilitarized buffer zone to physically separate adversarial forces.

title: Young Innovator Aims to 'Solve Ethiopia's Medical Oxygen Shortages'
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Mudhataa Bariisoo, a 30-year-old biomedical engineering technician at Adola Hospital in Guji, Southern Oromia Zone in Ethiopia, has developed a medical oxygen production and purification device aimed at addressing persistent oxygen shortages in Ethiopia's healthcare facilities.

title: Red Cross Warns of Worsening Humanitarian Crisis in Oromia
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has warned that the humanitarian situation in Ethiopia's Oromia region is deteriorating amid persistent armed conflict, deadly civilian attacks and growing displacement, saying it is struggling to reach all communities affected by the escalating insecurity.

title: PM Abiy Unveils 57-Hectare Urban Corridor Development Project in Addis Ababa
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has officially unveiled a 57-hectare urban corridor development project covering seven routes and connecting roads in Addis Ababa, aimed at transforming the capital into a more productive, inclusive and livable city.

title: Ethiopia's Future Peacekeeping Role Must Keep Balancing National Interests, Regional Duties - Navy Commandant
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia's future engagement in international peacekeeping must keep balancing national security interests, international obligations, and its enduring commitment to peace and stability in the Horn of Africa, FDRE Navy Commandant Vice Admiral Kindu Gezu stated.

title: Ethiopia Strengthens Pandemic Preparedness, Health Security, Minister Says
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has made significant progress in strengthening its health security and emergency response systems, raising its International Health Regulations (IHR) capacity score from 62 to 70, Minister of Health Dr. Mekdes Daba announced.

title: Ethiopia's Strengthened Defense Capacity Vital to National, Regional Security
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia's growing defense capabilities are strengthening the country's ability to safeguard its national interests and contribute to peace and stability across the region, Commandant of the International Peace Support Training Centre Gezahegn Fekadu said.

title: Ethiopia Steps Up Climate Diplomacy Ahead of COP32 in Addis Ababa
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia is intensifying its diplomatic engagement with international climate institutions and partners to build cooperation and secure support ahead of hosting the 32nd United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP32) in Addis Ababa in November 2027.

title: Power Without Transparency - Who Holds Ethiopia's Media Regulator Accountable When It Silences the Press?
summary: [Addis Standard] On 2 November 2026, the Ethiopian Media Authority (EMA) announced the indefinite suspension of the registration certificate of Media and Communication Center PLC, the publisher of the Amharic-language Reporter and the English-language The Reporter, and their digital platforms. One of Ethiopia's longest-established independent media organizations was brought to a halt. title: In-Depth Analysis - Emptied of Civilians, No End in Sight - How the Escalating Moyale Conflict Is Deepening a Humanitarian Crisis
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Once a bustling border town sustained by cross-border commerce, pastoralist livelihoods and closely interconnected communities, Moyale is increasingly being emptied of its civilian population as escalating clashes between Oromia and Somali regional forces drive residents from their homes, disrupt economic activity and push tens of thousands across the border into Kenya.

title: El Niño, Iran War Shocks Could Push Nearly One Million More Ethiopians Into Poverty, New Report Warns
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Nearly 905,000 additional people in Ethiopia could be pushed into poverty and 2.8 million into undernourishment in 2027 as the effects of a potentially exceptionally strong El Niño converge with higher global fuel prices linked to the Iran war, according to a new analysis by the International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI).

title: Ethiopia-Eritrea Border Clashes Raise Fears of Regional War
summary: [DW] As Ethiopian troops push Tigrayan forces toward the Eritrean border, fears of a new regional war are growing. With tensions rising between Ethiopia, Eritrea and Sudan, the Horn of Africa faces uncertain times ahead.

title: Ethiopia Calls for Scaled-Up, Accessible Climate Finance for Developing Countries
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Foreign Affairs Minister and COP32 President-Designate Gedion Timothewos has called for climate finance to be mobilized at the scale required, through accessible channels and in line with the priorities of developing countries.

title: Newly Appointed Ambassadors Vow to Strengthen, Expand Cooperation With Ethiopia
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Newly appointed ambassadors to Ethiopia have expressed their commitment to strengthening and expanding cooperation with the country in various spheres of collaboration.

title: Washington Protest Brings Horn of Africa Diaspora Over Ethiopia Conflicts, Regional Instability
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A coalition of Horn of Africa diaspora communities staged a protest outside the U.S. Department of State in Washington, D.C., on Monday, November 16, calling on the United States and the international community to intervene over ongoing conflicts in Ethiopia and mounting regional tensions.

title: Toyo Suspends Imports of Ethiopian-Made Solar Cells to U.S. Amid Ongoing Trade Probe
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Japanese solar manufacturer TOYO Co., Ltd. has suspended imports of solar cells produced at its Ethiopian facility into the United States, citing uncertainty surrounding an ongoing US Department of Commerce investigation into alleged tariff circumvention involving Chinese-origin components.

title: Salsay Weyane Tigray Warns of Famine-Driven Displacement in Tselemti, Calls for Halt to Revenge-Driven Actions
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Salsay Weyane Tigray, an opposition political group, has warned of worsening hunger and displacement in Lailay Tselemti Woreda, Northwestern Tigray, saying severe famine has forced residents to abandon their homes and migrate in search of survival, as the region faces mounting humanitarian pressures from drought, extreme weather and renewed conflict.

title: Alliance for Survival, Amhara Fano Leaders Urge UN Envoy to Facilitate Inclusive Political Dialogue in Ethiopia
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Leaders of the Alliance for Survival and the Amhara Fano National Movement (AFNM) have urged the United Nations to facilitate an inclusive political dialogue in Ethiopia, telling the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa that a credible peace process must address what they described as existential threats facing the Amhara population and the demands of Ethiopia's wider communities.

title: Beyond the Battlefield - How Strategic Centralization Deepens Somalia's Political, Security Crisis
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The most consequential victories Al-Shabaab has secured in recent years have not necessarily occurred on the battlefield. Some have emerged from political chambers, constitutional disputes, neglected rural communities, and the growing frustration of populations that once stood at the forefront of Somalia's fight against extremism.

title: President Taye Receives Credentials of 16 Ambassadors
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- President Taye Atske Selassie has received letters of credence of 16 newly appointed ambassadors to Ethiopia during an official diplomatic ceremony held at the National Palace today.

title: 'Hunger Should Not Be a Concern' - WFP Steps in for Families in Kenya Who Fled Ethiopia Violence
summary: [UN News] The World Food Programme (WFP) is assisting thousands of families who fled recent violence in Ethiopia for the Moyale area in neighbouring Kenya, the UN agency reported on Tuesday.

title: Africans Must Reclaim Cultural Narratives - Nebiyou
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- African scholars and institutions should take greater ownership of the study, interpretation and promotion of the continent's cultural heritage, Ethiopia's State Minister for Culture and Tourism, Nebiyou Baye has said.

title: Addis Ababa City Administration Reaffirms Commitment to Strengthening Partnership With WB Group
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- The Addis Ababa City Administration has reaffirmed its commitment to expanding development cooperation with the World Bank (WB) Group through joint projects aimed at promoting sustainable urban development and improving residents' quality of life.
